# URLCode store

> Operator-installed declarative data store extension for URLCode. Declare
> typed collections in `urlcode.yaml`, mount each with `extension: store`, and
> the extension serves a bounded JSON CRUD API backed by atomically written
> files in an operator-owned directory. No handler code. Installed with
> `urlcode extensions add store`; not an independent security assessment. Apache-2.0.

Part of the URLCode framework, in the same repository: docs/FRAMEWORK.md

## What a project declares (YAML only; never packages, code or credentials)
- `extensions.store: { version: "1", config: { collections: { <name>: { fields, sortable, filterable, readOnly, ... } } } }`
- A mount per collection, e.g. `/api/notes/*: { extension: store, methods: [GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE] }`
- Protect the mount with `auth: true` (the example adds it when auth is installed) unless the
  example's explicit `--ack store:public-write` was given; an unprotected write mount has no rate
  limiting, abuse protection or multi-tenant isolation of its own.
- Optional list-and-form screens: `extensions.store.config.screens: { /todos: { collection: todos, title?, columns? } }`
  plus a route `/todos/*: { extension: ui, methods: [GET, HEAD] }`. The store contributes them to the
  `ui` extension (`contributes.ui.screens`); they are declared here, never under `extensions.ui`.
- `urlcode extensions add store` writes an empty `collections` block and no mount; `--example`
  adds the `todos` collection on `/api/todos` (and the `/todos` screen when ui is installed); with
  auth installed the mount gets `auth: true` and the collection `ownership: owner` (per-user records).
- `ownership: owner` on a collection scopes every request to the principal a policy such as
  `auth: true` on its mount sets; without it (the default) a collection is shared. An owned
  collection may add `maxRecordsPerOwner: N` (at most `maxRecords`): a principal holding N records
  gets `409 owner_quota_exceeded`; `maxRecords` still caps the whole collection.
- With the server stopped, `urlcode-store reassign --directory <dir> --project <app> --from <id>
  --to <id> [--collection <name>] [--dry-run]` moves one principal's records to another (a
  rotated API key's records to its replacement); it refuses as a whole if `--to` would exceed
  a collection's `maxRecordsPerOwner`.
- The operator activates it in the site's `host.mjs` with `store()` (or `store({directory})`) in
  the `composeHost` list; `urlcode extensions add store` writes that line.

## Read in this order
- [README](README.md): install, scaffold, host options.
- [docs/STORE.md](../../docs/STORE.md): the full HTTP contract, limits and concurrency guarantees.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): trust boundary, locking, `ETag`/`If-Match`, `Idempotency-Key` scoping.

## Do not guess
- No CRUD or persistence code in project `function`/`middleware` routes; declare the
  collection. Those routes run trusted and in-process, but hold no store authority of their own.
- One server process per data directory (an exclusive lock file enforces it); no
  transactions, whole-file atomic writes, last write wins unless a caller sends `If-Match`.
- `sortable`/`filterable` field lists are declared per collection; `?sort=`/`?<field>=` queries
  against an undeclared name are `400`s, not silently ignored.
- The data directory is operator-owned, outside the project, on local disk, not a network
  filesystem; the store creates it `0700` and its files `0600`.
- The `store-schema` artifact is the configuration schema and an example as inert JSON:
  adding it does not register `store` or grant data access.
